reason: Researched with WebSearch (budget was still live, so this is real research, not a packet-only call) and every leg came back confirmed rather than contradicted. The leg is three sessions old (filled 09-30) and no company-specific news has arrived for any of the five names since that fill. V: core payment volumes at records and stablecoin settlement up 15x year-over-year, with the 09-30 Open Standard/OUSD consortium putting Visa on the issuing side of the disintermediation it is supposed to fear; the DOJ antitrust and swipe-fee overhang is real but unchanged and already priced into a 22% weight. NVDA: new all-time high, ~$5.7T cap, Morgan Stanley reinstated it as top semi pick; the circular-deal/OpenAI-financing critique is the live bear case and is exactly why it is 20% and not 30%, with a -20% stop. TSM: AI demand described as exceptionally strong, FY26 capex raised to $60-64B, Q3 prints 10-15 with a quiet period opening 10-05 - I am not resizing into a blackout. CME: record September AND record Q3 average daily volume across rates, equities, energy, ags, FX, metals and crypto, earnings 10-21; the thesis that CME earns more from the rate volatility that threatens the rest of the book is the one leg this week's macro actively validated. GOOGL at 14% is the one name that fails my own stated screen - 2026 capex guided to $195-205B, Q2 free cash flow of -$5.9B, zero buyback, $49.6B of stock/convertible preferred and $20.3B of notes issued - but that is precisely why I already halved it on 09-30 and it is not new information. Finishing that exit now would mean I misjudged three days ago, not that anything changed; the honest trigger is Q3 in late October showing a second negative-FCF quarter, and until then the -18% stop enforces the discipline for me. The only genuinely new information this week is macro: cooler-than-expected PCE on 10-01 and a 29K September payroll print on 10-02 collapsed October Fed HIKE odds from ~70% to ~17%, while a December hike stays priced. That setup is mildly good for this book as constructed - lower yields support the long-duration franchises, the live December debate keeps CME's volume engine running - and the stalling labour market is the one argument for trimming V, which I am noting rather than acting on at a 22% weight with records in the underlying business. 17% cash at 4% is the right dry powder into a TSM print on 10-15 and a contested December FOMC. Decisive mechanical reason not to churn: this schema only permits HOLD or a full replacement book, so moving a single stop would re-register all five legs at the 10-05 close, discarding a favourable basis (NVDA +2.44%, TSM +3.64%, V +0.37%, CME +0.44%) and re-anchoring every stop and take-profit to a higher fill. A quality-compounder mandate on leg 9 of its history does not need a tenth leg to re-price its own stops upward for no new reason.
